what: Ryan Specialty is a wholesale insurance broker. When a risk is too unusual for a standard insurer, the retail broker brings it to Ryan, which places it with specialty and surplus lines carriers and takes a commission.
customers: Retail insurance brokers placing hard-to-insure risks, and the specialty carriers that write them.
money: placing specialty risks with surplus lines carriers
small specialty risks bound directly under delegated authority
moat: Relationships on both sides of a market that only works through intermediaries: retail brokers bring the hard risks, carriers trust the submission quality, and neither side changes partner easily.
risks: $3.5B of debt from an acquisition programme, against $158M of cash
60 times earnings because acquisition amortisation depresses the accounting profit
Specialty insurance pricing is softening, and commissions move with premium rates
opportunities: $569M of free cash flow against $105M of reported net income, so cash is far better than earnings
Revenue grew from $1.4B to $3.1B in four years
Risks keep moving out of the standard market into specialty, which is exactly this business
watch: Organic revenue growth separate from acquisitions.
